skill.name: chrome-devtools
skill.description: Provides command patterns for controlling Chrome through chrome-devtools-mcp to debug pages, inspect console and network activity, capture screenshots, evaluate page JavaScript, and automate simple browser interactions.
skill.summary: Control Chrome through chrome-devtools-mcp for web debugging and browser automation.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline examples, reserved test URLs, loopback addresses, documentation links, and /dev/null redirection. The real concerns are unpinned remote package execution through bunx and exposure of sensitive browser content through DevTools screenshots, snapshots, console logs, and network inspection. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration endpoint was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin chrome-devtools-mcp to a reviewed version and document the trusted package source before recommending repeated use.
Default to isolated browser profiles, test accounts, and explicit user consent before screenshots, snapshots, network logs, or existing Chrome attachment.
Replace broad force-kill examples with targeted shutdown guidance or a confirmation step before terminating matching processes.

- Use `-- --isolated` to create temporary profile (prevents browser lock conflicts)

- ❌ `list_pages` - Broken, use `navigate_page` or `new_page` instead (they return page list)

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly recommends executing chrome-devtools-mcp from npm through bunx using the latest package tag. That creates a supply-chain risk because future package changes execute without version review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple documented commands execute chrome-devtools-mcp at runtime through bunx with an unpinned latest tag. This is a clear supply-chain exposure, although the intent is legitimate browser debugging.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Browser Data Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill enables screenshots, page snapshots, console logs, network activity review, and optional attachment to an existing Chrome debug endpoint. These capabilities can expose credentials, session data, private page content, or request details if used on sensitive pages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The listed DevTools operations directly access browser-visible data, and the file itself warns that the server exposes full browser content. The behavior is expected for debugging, so the risk is contextual rather than malicious.

content.value_statement: Browser debugging often needs repeatable console, network, page, and screenshot checks. This skill provides command patterns for chrome-devtools-mcp so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can inspect pages through Chrome.
actual_capabilities: Launch chrome-devtools-mcp through the mcp CLI and bunx.
Navigate Chrome to local or remote URLs for inspection.
List browser console messages and network requests.
Capture screenshots and page snapshots for debugging.
Evaluate page JavaScript and interact with forms.
Connect to an existing Chrome debugging endpoint when configured.
limitations: Requires shell access plus the mcp CLI and bunx runtime.
Recommended commands execute a package from npm at runtime unless the version is pinned.
Browser snapshots, screenshots, console logs, and network data can include sensitive information.
It is a DevTools workflow guide, not a full replacement for Playwright or Selenium test suites.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Local App Errors
use_cases.description: Open a localhost app, collect console messages, and identify browser-side failures during development.

use_cases.title: Capture UI Evidence
use_cases.description: Take screenshots and page snapshots to document visual defects, missing content, or broken interactions.

use_cases.title: Inspect Network Behavior
use_cases.description: Review page requests and browser logs while testing loading states, API failures, or third-party resources.

prompt_templates.title: Check Console Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner debugging for a local page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open my local web app at the URL I provide. List console errors and summarize the most likely cause.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Network Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of failed page requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to this page, inspect network requests, and report failed or suspicious requests with a short explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Page Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Documenting a visual or content issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Take a full-page screenshot and page snapshot, then summarize visible layout issues and missing content.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Interaction Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation of a user journey.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an isolated Chrome session to load the app, perform the interaction steps I provide, inspect console and network activity, and report relevant findings only.

output_examples.input: Check why my local app shows a blank screen.
output: Opened the local app in an isolated Chrome session.
Reported the browser console errors and failing requests.
Summarized the most likely client-side cause.

output_examples.input: Capture evidence for a broken checkout page.
output: Captured a page screenshot and a readable page snapshot.
Identified visible layout problems and missing interactive elements.
Noted that sensitive user data should be removed before sharing results.

output_examples.input: Review network activity after submitting a form.
output: Loaded the page and performed the requested interaction.
Listed failed requests, unexpected redirects, and relevant console messages.
Provided a concise debugging summary for the next code review.

best_practices: Use isolated Chrome sessions and test accounts for all browser inspection tasks.
Pin and review external tool versions before repeated or automated use.
Set command timeouts and close browser-control sessions after each task.
anti_patterns: Attaching the tool to a personal Chrome profile with active sessions.
Running remote packages marked as latest in production workflows without review.
Capturing screenshots, snapshots, or network logs from pages that contain secrets.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Chrome DevTools workflows through chrome-devtools-mcp, including navigation, console review, network inspection, screenshots, and page snapshots.

faq.question: Does it require local tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow expects shell access, the mcp CLI, bunx, and a Chrome-compatible browser environment.

faq.question: Can it debug localhost pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples focus on localhost development pages and can also navigate to test or documentation sites.

faq.question: Can it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It can capture page screenshots, but users should avoid pages that show private data or credentials.

faq.question: Is it safe with logged-in sites?
faq.answer: Use caution. Prefer isolated sessions and test accounts because DevTools access can expose page content, cookies, console data, and requests.

faq.question: Does it replace browser test frameworks?
faq.answer: No. It is best for interactive debugging and inspection, while Playwright or Selenium are better for maintained test suites.
